attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post, addressed to tech workers.

semantics.note: The draft captures the firm present-tense claim about capabilities. Splitting off the separate clause about enthusiasts' motives is reasonable. No hedge applies.

contract.note: In context, reading the promise as agent autonomy plus less human effort is an ordinary reading. May 2026 is a reasonable window. The promises themselves are unspecified, so the result depends on which promises are matched.

evidence.note: April 2026 Anthropic statement. It describes agent capabilities and admitted risks, which helps frame the promises. It is not May 2026 performance evidence.

Anthropic reports a 76% success rate on its own internal open-ended tasks in May 2026. This is a company disclosure on tasks it selected itself, not checked independently or matched to public promises. It points against the claim but does not settle it.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no independent comparison of public promises against May 2026 performance and net human effort. Anthropic's internal success figures point the other way but are its own measurements on tasks it chose. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The scored part is the firm forecast that the money will not last forever. The present-tense lines about plans and products are premises. No deadline was stated.

contract.note: The contract fairly requires a decisive, industry-wide capital exhaustion and sets no deadline. The industry's membership and the meaning of 'losing' are not defined, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 (Oct 26, 2026) says it still depends on access to capital. That is one firm's risk disclosure, not industry-wide exhaustion.
Announcement that the S-1 was filed; the IPO is pending, not completed. It does not resolve the industry-wide forecast.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and the packet shows no decisive industry-wide financing failure and no durable self-financing. One firm's disclosures of capital dependence and a pending IPO do not meet the early-resolution rule. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The draft correctly keeps 'only real outcome' and the 'appears to be' hedge. 'Appears' is graded epistemic confidence, not a firm assertion, so under policy the claim is not scored.

contract.note: The contract scores the claim on a plain reading even though it is hedged ('appears to be'). The plain-reading rule covers only firm language. 'Small fraction' and 'real outcome' are also undefined.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement of $122B in committed capital. Committed is not the same as received, and it does not show that hyperscaler revenue depends on that money.
Anthropic's S-1 shows large Q1 2026 net losses, much of them from fair-value changes on financing instruments. Relevant to 'unprofitable', but the claim is hedged and not scored.
Microsoft discloses a $37B annual AI revenue run rate. That is an annualised figure with no customer split, so it is not realized revenue matched to capital spending.

reviews.rationale: Zitron hedged the claim: the only real outcome 'appears to be' propping up the two labs. Under policy, graded confidence like this is not scored. Even if it were, the packet has no reconciled numbers on capex, revenue and financing.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the named GPU types and the author's estimate. 'I estimate' gives the measurement basis for the 20% figure and is not a probability hedge. The exclusivity claim ('only revenue') is firm.

contract.note: Reading 'only revenue' as literal exclusivity is strict for rhetorical prose but plausible. Whether the 20% applies to each provider or to the three combined, and what counts as cloud revenue, would decide the result.

evidence.note: Amazon reports Q1 2026 AWS sales of $37.6B. That gives a denominator but no figure for the two labs' spending.

Google says it supports H100s in Dataflow and names other customers using GPUs there. That weighs against exclusivity, but it does not tie those customers to the named GPU models or show paid use in Q1 2026.

reviews.rationale: The packet has neither of the two labs' spending at any provider, so the 20% share cannot be tested. Google's Dataflow post suggests other customers use GPUs, but it does not show revenue on the named GPU models in the target quarter. The evidence settles neither part of the claim.
